purpose: The ten poruthams exactly as the Sudamani Ullamudaiyan edition prints them (பொருத்தவியல், verses 183-199), transcribed so tamilPorutham.js can be compared against a primary text instead of against itself. This is a TRANSCRIPTION of one source. It is not a claim that this source is the only tradition, nor that its rules are the ones practitioners should follow.

source.title: சூடாமணி உள்ளமுடையான் : உரையுடன் (சோதிட நூல்)
source.author: ஓலைச்சுவடி மூலம்; தஞ்சாவூர் சரசுவதி மகால் நூலகப் பதிப்பு

verification.VISUAL: Read from the rendered page image, digit by digit and name by name.
verification.INFERRED_FROM_VERSE: Not in the printed commentary; supplied by the verse itself. Flagged individually below.
verification.OCR_ONLY: Taken from the OCR text and not looked at. None remain in this file.

DINA.rule: Favourable counts, counted from the woman's star to the man's. The commentary prints the list; how the count continues past the first ten ('இவை பத்தும் சென்றால் அவை தொட்டு எண்ணுவது') is not explained, and 29 exceeds the 27 stars.

sameStar.note: When the woman and man share a star (count 1) the book grades by the star instead.
sameStar.madhyamaNote: Anuradha (16) is inferred from the verse: the printed commentary names only eight of the nine.

GANA.rule: Same gana: uttama. Manushya with Deva: madhyama. Rakshasa with Deva: quarrel (சிலுகு). Rakshasa with Manushya: death (மரணம்).
GANA.devaNote: Pushya (7) is inferred from the verse ('தலைபூ சங்கள்'); the printed commentary lists only eight Deva stars while saying nine.
GANA.rakshasaNote: Magha (9) is inferred from the verse ('மகம்கணம் அரக்கர்க்'); the printed commentary lists only eight Rakshasa stars while saying nine.

MAHENDRA.rule: Favourable counts from the woman's star to the man's.
MAHENDRA.note: The commentary prints 20. The verse's own arithmetic ('ஒன்றொழித் திருபான்' = 19, then 'ஐந்தும் இருபத்தோ டிரண்டும்' = 25 and 22) does not obviously give it. Recorded as printed.

STREE_DEERGHA.rule: Count from the woman's star to the man's; thirteen or more is good.

YONI.rule: A different model from a numeric grouping. Each star has an animal and a sex. Verse 191 names enemy animals; verse 192 grades by the sexes: both male is enmity (பகை), both female is uttama, and the two mixed cases are both good.
YONI.gaps: Anuradha's animal is missing from the printed commentary, and the sex of the two snakes is not stated, so a faithful implementation cannot be completed from this edition alone.

RASI.rule: Count from the woman's rasi to the man's. The seventh or beyond is uttama; fewer than seven is not acceptable.

RASI_ADHIPATHI.rule: A friendship table keyed on the woman's rasi ('இவை ஸ்திரீ இராசிகளுக்குப் பொருத்தம்'): the man's rasi must be one of the listed friends.
RASI_ADHIPATHI.note: Mithuna and Kanni: 'சிங்கம் ஒழிய எல்லாம் உறவு' — every rasi except Simha (4).

VASYA.rule: A table of which rasis are drawn to which. Not symmetric in the book (Mithuna lists Kanni; Kanni lists Rishaba and Meena).

RAJJU.rule: Both in the same rajju band is not acceptable. Consequences differ by band: foot loses wealth, thigh means a barren wife, belly means the children die, neck means the husband dies, head means the wife dies.

VEDHA.rule: Pairs that are mutually incompatible, plus one triple. All other stars are compatible.
VEDHA.tripleNote: அசுபதி, மகம், மூலம் இவை தம்மில் பொருந்தாது — none of the three is compatible with either of the others.
